# Real analysis in Litex, setting-first.
#
# Included: epsilon tails, sequence limits and convergence, constant-sequence
# convergence, uniqueness of limits, and a uniquely defined limit selector.
#
# Main line: epsilon tails -> convergence -> uniqueness of a sequence limit.
# Sequences here are functions on N+, retaining the original one-based domain.
# Write that carrier explicitly instead of relying on the migrating seq alias.

prop is_tail_close_to(a fn(index N+) R, L R, epsilon R+, n0 N+):
    forall n N+:
        n >= n0
        =>:
            |a(n) - L| < epsilon

prop has_eventual_closeness_to(a fn(index N+) R, L R, epsilon R+):
    exist n0 N+ st {$is_tail_close_to(a, L, epsilon, n0)}

prop has_limit(a fn(index N+) R, L R):
    forall epsilon R+:
        $has_eventual_closeness_to(a, L, epsilon)

prop is_convergent_sequence(a fn(index N+) R):
    exist L R st {$has_limit(a, L)}

# A constant sequence is eventually epsilon-close immediately, with n0 = 1.

template<c R>:
    have fn constant_sequence(n N+) R = c

thm constant_sequence_has_limit:
    ? forall c R:
        $has_limit(\constant_sequence<c>, c)
    claim:
        ? forall epsilon R+:
            $has_eventual_closeness_to(\constant_sequence<c>, c, epsilon)
        claim:
            ? forall n N+:
                n >= 1
                =>:
                    |\constant_sequence<c>(n) - c| < epsilon
            \constant_sequence<c>(n) = c
            \constant_sequence<c>(n) - c = 0
            |\constant_sequence<c>(n) - c| = 0
            0 < epsilon
            |\constant_sequence<c>(n) - c| < epsilon
        by def $is_tail_close_to(\constant_sequence<c>, c, epsilon, 1)
        witness $has_eventual_closeness_to(\constant_sequence<c>, c, epsilon) from 1
    by def $has_limit(\constant_sequence<c>, c)
    $has_limit(\constant_sequence<c>, c)

# Keep witness construction in a claim, then close the contradiction with facts.
# The common tail index n1 + n2 is at least each positive starting index.
